newsitem.title: ECUADOR: Black box found after U.S. jet hits Ecuador city.
newsitem.headline: Black box found after U.S. jet hits Ecuador city.

text.p: Ecuador's air force has located the black box flight recorder of a U.S. cargo jet that burst into flames and crashed into the port of Manta, killing 25 people and injuring 60, officials said on Thursday.

The black box was found in charred ruins in the poor Dolorosa neighborhood where the Millon Air Boeing 707 crashed on Tuesday night, showering burning wreckage and jet fuel over eight densely populated blocks of the Pacific port.

Manta fire chief Eliecer Alatis said the death toll rose to 25 after two more people died of their burns and said more bodies could still be found. "We are still sifting through the rubble. We hope to finish today," he said.

As Ecuador began three days of national mourning ordered by President Abadala Bucaram, authorities in the port city 290 miles (480 km) southeast of Quito, which had been planning a local fiesta this week, urged bereaved families to bury their dead immediately for health reasons.

Emergency services prepared to flatten the four blocks of Dolorosa -- Spanish for "painful" -- that bore the brunt of the crash, including a church that took a direct hit and protected some neighboring buildings from damage. Locals said a statue of the Virgin Mary miraculously escaped harm.

The Boeing 707-300, bound for Miami with a cargo of frozen fish and flowers, burst into flames 10 minutes after takeoff from Manta airport. Its burning wings and fuselage tore tin roofs off houses and smashed others to rubble. Rescuers had to wait for daybreak before searching for bodies because the plane ripped out electricity lines as it crashed.

The black box will be sent to the United States to help determine the cause of the tragedy and wreckage was taken to Manta airport for study by experts from engine makers Pratt & Whitney and the U.S. National Transportation Safety Board.
Ecuadoran newspaper Hoy reported that the Millon Air plane experienced engine problems twice last week, forcing it once to abort take-off and another time to return after take-off.

Millon is a Miami-based carrier owned by Colombians that operates charter freight flights to Latin America. In April 1995, a Millon DC-8 overran a runway in Guatemala City and crashed into a shantytown, killing six people on the ground.
